FOOTNOTES

1/ In addition to the operating lump sum appropriation, an amount equal to the revenue share agreement with the United States forest service for Fool Hollow Lake recreation area and Catalina state park is appropriated to the Arizona state parks board from the state parks revenue fund established by section 41-511.21, Arizona Revised Statutes. (General Appropriations Act footnote)

2/ General Appropriations Act funds are appropriated as an Operating Lump Sum with Special Line Items by Agency.

Operating Budget

The Baseline includes \$17,446,500 and 133.2 FTE Positions in FY 2027 for the operating budget. These amounts consist of:

State Parks Revenue Fund (SPRF) \$17,429,800

Off-Highway Vehicle Recreation Fund 16,700

Adjustments are as follows:

Remove One-Time Family Campout Costs

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(231,000) from SPRF in FY 2027 for removal of one-time equipment costs associated with expanding the Family Campout Program, which teaches basic camping skills to families with little to no camping experience.

Arizona State Parks Heritage Fund Deposit

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for the Arizona State Parks Heritage Fund Deposit line item. Adjustments are as follows:
section_path: Arizona State Parks Heritage Fund Deposit

text:
Remove One-Time Deposit

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(1,000,000) from the General Fund in FY 2027 for removal of a one-time deposit into the Arizona State Parks Heritage Fund.

Pursuant to a General Appropriations Act footnote, FY 2026 monies in this line item may not be used to purchase property.

Arizona Trail Fund Deposit

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for the Arizona Trail Fund Deposit line item. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

Monies in the Arizona Trail Fund are for the sole purpose of maintaining and preserving the Arizona trail. The Arizona Trail is an 800 mile-long, non-motorized trail beginning at the U.S.-Mexican border and running northsouth through the state into Utah.

This project was funded on a one-time basis in FY 2022 through FY 2025 at varying levels.

Broadband Infrastructure Operations and Maintenance

The Baseline includes \$242,100 from SPRF in FY 2027 for the Broadband Infrastructure Operations and

Maintenance line item. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

Monies in this line item are used to pay ongoing operations and maintenance costs associated with broadband internet projects at several state parks. The projects were originally funded by federal American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) monies.

Kartchner Caverns State Park

The Baseline includes \$2,587,700 and 35.8 FTE Positions from SPRF in FY 2027 for Kartchner Caverns State Park. These amounts are unchanged from FY 2026.

Kartchner Caverns is located in Benson, Arizona and was discovered in 1974. The State Parks Board acquired the property in 1988 and opened the caverns to the public in 1999.

State Lake Improvement Fund Deposit

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for the State Lake Improvement Fund Deposit line item. Adjustments are as follows:

Remove One-Time Deposit

The Baseline includes a decrease of \$(1,500,000) from the General Fund in FY 2027 for removal of a one-time deposit into the State Lake Improvement Fund.

Monies in the State Lake Improvement Fund are used to fund projects at boating sites, including launching ramps, parking areas, lake improvement and construction, campgrounds, and acquisition of property to provide access to boating sites.

State Parks Store

The Baseline includes \$1,530,200 from the State Park Store Fund in FY 2027 for the State Parks Store line item. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

Monies in the State Parks Store line item are used to operate and maintain state-owned giftshops.

Veterans Memorial Park Feasibility Study

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for a Veterans Memorial Park Feasibility Study. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

The FY 2024 budget included \$10,000,000 from SPRF to purchase land for a new Arizona Veterans Memorial Park. Monies in this line item fund a study to evaluate the feasibility of constructing various proposed facilities on the land purchased with the FY 2024 appropriation.

Veterans Memorial Park Purchase

The Baseline includes no funding in FY 2027 for a Veterans Memorial Park Purchase. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

Laws 2023, Chapter 199 appropriated \$10,000,000 from SPRF in FY 2024 to establish a new state park near the Arizona Veterans National Cemetery in Cave Creek. Chapter 199 also allows the board to enter into an Intergovernmental Agreement with Maricopa County for the maintenance and preservation of the park and requires ASPB to receive approval from the Joint Committee on Capital Review for the design and construction of the park.

The FY 2026 budget extended the lapsing date of the \$10,000,000 appropriation to June 30, 2027.

Water and Wastewater Infrastructure Operations and Maintenance

The Baseline includes \$541,000 from SPRF in FY 2027 for the Water and Wastewater Infrastructure Operations and

Maintenance line item. This amount is unchanged from FY 2026.

Monies in this line item fund ongoing operations and maintenance costs associated with wastewater projects at several state parks. The projects were originally funded by federal ARPA monies.

Other Issues

State Parks Operations

As of November 2025, 30 state parks and natural areas are open to the public. Twenty-six parks are funded and operated by the state with existing state funds. Four open parks are operated through agreements between the State Parks Board and local governments. (Please see the State Parks Visitation and Revenue Program Summary available on the JLBC website for additional information on the parks, visitation, and operations.)

Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Fund (PRA2985/U.S. P.L. 117-2)

Federal Funds

Source of Revenue: Federal monies appropriated in the American Rescue Plan Act (P.L. 117-2). Purpose of Fund: To provide emergency support to households, small businesses, nonprofits, workers performing essential work, and certain industries negatively impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic. To extend government services that received a reduction in revenue as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic. To make investments in water, sewer, and broadband infrastructure.
